prompt.text: Use code 1 for a table, 2 for a bar graph, 3 for a pictogram, 4 for a line graph and 5 for a pie chart. A coach has the lap time and heart rate of a player for each of 12 training sessions, and players must find the exact pair of numbers for any session. For the reason code, use 1 if a line graph cannot be used for time data, 2 if a line graph can show only one measure, or 3 if a line graph would make readers estimate each exact pair of numbers from the points. Enter a two-digit number: the first digit is the code of the most suitable display and the second digit is the reason code.

content.text: Decide what players must do with the numbers.
Each session has two exact measurements. Choose the display that keeps both exact numbers for every session, then think about what players would have to do if they used a line graph instead.
A table keeps the exact pair of numbers for each of the 12 sessions. On a line graph players would have to estimate each exact pair from the points, so the reason code is 3.
